from pypdf import PdfReader

r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')

parts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    parts.append(f'\\n\\n=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n\\n'+p.extract_text())
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts)[:36000])
PY"

from pathlib import Path
for i in range(1, 11):
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.png').unlink()
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').unlink()
print('Removed temporary PDF inspection files.')
PY"

strengths: LPAM addresses a practical stitching problem through targeted repair of poorly aligned seam segments. Its modular, training-free design could be useful for improving existing pipelines without replacing their initial alignment methods.

Tables 1–2 show consistent average improvements across three datasets totaling 79 image pairs, testing four seam-cutters under REW and five initial alignment methods with baseline seam-cutting. For example, baseline SSIM on SEAGULL improves from 0.638 to 0.697. The visual examples also demonstrate useful local corrections.

The pipeline and algorithm are understandable, the principal components and existing datasets are cited, and a code link is provided. Parameter ablations and the explicit failure example help explain the tradeoff between alignment accuracy and smooth patch integration.
weaknesses: The quantitative evaluation does not adequately establish overall mosaic quality. All four metrics in Eqs. (6–9) measure agreement in neighborhoods along the selected seam and can miss distortion or artifacts elsewhere. Table 3 exposes this limitation: removing the sigmoid improves most metrics, including SEAGULL SSIM from 0.697 to 0.768, despite introducing visible boundary artifacts. Dataset-wide perceptual or structural evaluation is needed to substantiate the central smoothness benefit.

The contribution is insufficiently distinguished from existing seam-guided alignment and dense-matching approaches, including [22] and [35]. The modular post-processing arrangement is useful, but the broad claims of a new paradigm and independence from initial alignment exceed the demonstrated advance. Quantitative comparisons against complete SEAGULL/Parallax systems and a straightforward dense-flow refinement baseline would better establish the benefit of the proposed selective repair strategy.

The seam-quality gate in Section 3.2 can accept a uniformly poor seam. For example, Q = 0.8 everywhere satisfies max(Q) <= 1.5 mean(Q), so refinement is skipped despite severe disagreement. This makes the method dependent on errors appearing as localized outliers; the experiments do not characterize this limitation as initial alignment deteriorates.

The claimed boundary consistency is not guaranteed by Eqs. (4–5). With beta = 8, the sigmoid endpoints are approximately 0.018 and 0.982, and a horizontal taper does not enforce continuity along all patch boundaries. Fixing boundary labels during seam merging preserves image ownership but does not ensure geometric continuity. The disclosed failure case is helpful, but aggregate evidence about introduced artifacts is missing.

Reproducibility remains incomplete in the supplied manuscript despite the code link. Alignment-patch padding and minimum sizes, overlapping-patch handling, and SIFT-flow settings are insufficiently specified. Runtime is reported without image resolutions or patch-count distributions, limiting assessment of the claimed computational efficiency.
